sections.label: Bill coverage of platform workers
sections.summary: The Bill covers self-employed persons providing delivery or ride-hail services with platform operators, protecting over 90% of such persons, but not other services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Currently, the Bill only covers self-employed persons who work with platform operators to provide two types of services, namely, delivery or ride-hail services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It does not cover self-employed persons who work with platform operators to provide other types of services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I understand that the Bill already protects more than 90% of self-employed persons who use online matching platforms through its coverage of delivery or ride-hail services.

sections.label: Platform workers lack employee protections
sections.summary: Platform workers are not employees and do not receive protections under the Employment Act, wrongful dismissal guidelines, workplace fairness legislation and TAFEP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Platform workers are not employees and do not receive the protections afforded by the Employment Act, the Tripartite Guidelines on Wrongful Dismissal, the Workplace Fairness Legislation and the Tripartite Guidelines for Fair Employment Practices (TAFEP).

sections.label: European Parliament Platform Work Directive
sections.summary: In April 2024, the European Parliament adopted the Platform Work Directive requiring platforms to give workers written information about automated monitoring and decision-making systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, in April 2024, the European Parliament adopted the Platform Work Directive, which required platforms to provide workers with written information about the automated monitoring and decision-making systems that it uses.

sections.label: Number of platform workers in Singapore
sections.summary: According to MOM's latest labour force report, there were 70,500 platform workers in Singapore in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to the latest labour force report by MOM, in 2023, there were 70,500 platform workers in Singapore.

sections.label: CPF Transition Support for platform workers
sections.summary: The change brings platform workers closer to par with employees, and the Government will fully cover their CPF payments in the first year, so take-home pay is not impacted in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The change for platform workers brings them closer to par with employees, which is a good thing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I also welcome the enhancements to the Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS), where the Government will fully cover platform workers' CPF payments in the first year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This means that platform workers’ take-home pay will not be impacted in 2025.

sections.label: CPF status in job-matching algorithms
sections.summary: The question asks how the Government will ensure a platform worker's CPF contribution status is never a relevant factor in a job-matching algorithm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, how will the Government ensure that a platform worker's CPF contribution status is never a relevant factor in a job-matching algorithm?

sections.label: Abuse cases against drivers
sections.summary: In 2023, over 200 abuse cases against taxi and private-hire drivers were reported.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2023 alone, there were more than 200 reported cases of abuse against taxi and private-hire drivers.

sections.label: Harassment protection gap
sections.summary: Platform workers are not protected against harassment under the proposed Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Yet, platform workers are not protected against harassment under the proposed Bill.

sections.label: Platform service definitions and coverage
sections.summary: Definitions are broad, but the First Schedule limits covered platform services to delivery and ride-hail.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The meanings of platform service, platform operator and platform worker are drafted broadly enough to potentially apply to a wide range of services, such as caregiving services and cleaning services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, based on the First Schedule, the two platform services covered in the Bill are limited to delivery service and ride-hail service for now.

sections.label: Locum nurses as platform workers
sections.summary: Locum nurses would fall within the platform worker definition, being subject to platform operators' management control.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Locum nurses would fall within the definition of platform workers, as they are similarly subject to the management control of platform operators.

sections.label: Bill aims to close gap
sections.summary: The Bill aims to close the gap between platform workers and traditional workplace counterparts, hoped to be a start.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The proposed Bill aims to close the gap between platform workers and their counterparts in a traditional workplace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As we roll out the new measures, I hope that this is just the start of broader efforts to scale up protections and uplift more platform workers.

sections.label: Bill reforms and financial balance
sections.summary: The Bill proposes CPF contributions, WICA extension and safety measures, staggering rates over five years with PCTS support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It is clear from this Bill that the Government has captured this balance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This Bill proposes much-needed reforms, including mandatory CPF contributions, extending Work Injury Compensation Act (WICA) and requiring platform operators to take reasonable measures to ensure the safety and health of their platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Bill recognises that the reforms are important, but so is the real financial impact on platform workers, platform operators and potentially consumers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Thus, for example, the Bill staggers contribution rates over five years and is supplemented by the PCTS, enhanced a few days ago to fully cover the increase in platform workers' CPF contributions in 2025.

sections.label: Employer contribution cost impact
sections.summary: With a 60% fixed expense deduction ratio, the 17% employers' contribution equals 6.8% of income, two thirds of the platform operator's topline.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: With the fixed expense deduction ratio of 60% for drivers, the employers' contribution, which is 17% of the platform worker's income, would be 6.8%, or two thirds of the topline of the platform operator.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Therefore, having the platform operator bear the full employers' contribution would mean reducing their revenue to about 3% of what it used to be.

sections.label: Withholding CPF contributions mechanics
sections.summary: The passage asks how platform operators will withhold the platform worker's CPF contribution given differing rates by income and age.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Given the differences in CPF contribution rates by income and by age, how will the withholding of the platform worker's contribution by the platform operators work?

sections.label: Relief for lower-income platform workers
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Senior Minister of State would consider temporary relief or adjusted contribution requirements for lower-income platform workers who cannot cope.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Second, while the phased implementation and enhanced PCTS will greatly help in mitigating the immediate burden on platform workers, will the Senior Minister of State be open to temporary relief measures or adjustments to contribution requirements in future for lower-income platform workers who simply cannot cope under the lower take-home pay?

sections.label: Transparent passing on of costs
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Senior Minister of State will ensure platform operators pass on costs transparently, without profiteering, and efficiently amid staggered CPF roll-out.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: How will the Senior Minister of State ensure that any passing on of costs to consumers by the platform operators is done in a way that is transparent and does not inadvertently create opportunities for profiteering, as well as in a way that is efficient, especially as the staggered roll-out of CPF contributions would lead to several rounds of this?

sections.label: Monitoring policy change impacts
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Government will monitor the policy changes' effectiveness and impacts, including CPF take-up, gig jobs, flexibility, business sustainability and consumer cost.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: How will the Government monitor the effectiveness and impacts of these policy changes, including the take-up rate for CPF contributions, the impact on the number of gig jobs, the impact on flexibility for platform workers, the impact on business sustainability for platform operators and the impact on consumer cost?

sections.label: Lapsed Home Protection Scheme cover
sections.summary: Because he had not made regular CPF contributions, he had not kept up Home Protection Scheme payments and the cover had lapsed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Because he had not been making regular CPF contributions, he had not kept up with his Home Protection Scheme (HPS) payments, and the cover had lapsed.

sections.label: CPF employer contribution for platform workers
sections.summary: The 17% employer CPF contribution increases CPF available for housing and helps platform workers save for a house or retirement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The employer contribution of CPF, at 17%, significantly increases the amount of CPF available for housing, and will help platform workers save for a house more quickly or save for retirement.

sections.label: Food delivery rider's monthly CPF contributions
sections.summary: Due to a major health condition, he has contributed $200 monthly to CPF since starting work as a food delivery rider.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Because of his brush with a major health condition, he has been making CPF contributions of $200 a month since he started work as a food delivery rider.

sections.label: Mr K welcomes proposed amendments
sections.summary: Mr K looks forward to the proposed amendments, especially the employer CPF contribution, WICA, and greater representation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Mr K looks forward to the proposed amendments, in particular the employer CPF contribution, WICA, and the prospect of greater representation.

sections.label: Bill recognises platform workers as key players
sections.summary: The Bill formalises platform workers as key economic players, letting associations negotiate collectively, represent disputes and support them, aiming for stability and productivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill before the House recognises them and formalises them as key players in our economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill is an important milestone for the community of platform workers because the various associations currently representing them would be able to negotiate collectively for them, better represent them in disputes and provide them with better support services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By strengthening worker protection, this Bill paves the way for a more stable and satisfied workforce, with expected outcomes, such as enhanced productivity and reduced turnover in sectors heavily reliant on gig and platform-based work.

sections.label: Compliance may raise platform operators' costs
sections.summary: The concern is that complying with the new regulations might increase operational costs for platform operators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My concern is that compliance with the new regulations might increase operational costs for platform operators.

sections.label: MOM division for gig economy needs
sections.summary: It asks if there are plans for a separate MOM division for gig economy needs, noting platform workers fell from 88,400 to 70,500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, are there any plans for a separate division within MOM to address the needs of the gig economy for the long term?

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   The number of Singapore platform workers in Singapore fell from 88,400 to 70,500 last year, accounting for 2.9% of our resident labour force.

sections.label: Expanding Bill to other sectors
sections.summary: Asks what process or mechanism exists to potentially expand the Bill's coverage to emerging platform services like cleaning and caregiving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With other emerging and growing platform services, such as cleaning and caregiving that may either presently or in the near future meet the same defined criteria, what process or mechanism is in place to potentially expand the coverage of the Bill to these sectors?

sections.label: Monitoring SMEs on cost increases
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government will monitor SMEs on the ground to ensure cost increases from the Platform Workers Bill are managed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Based on the recent Singapore Business Federation National Business Survey, nearly half of businesses remain uncertain about their future prospects, with 33% of SMEs and 24% of large companies reporting declining performance over the last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will the Government be actively monitoring SMEs on the ground to ensure that any cost increases resulting from the Platform Workers Bill are effectively managed?

sections.label: Bill restricts platform services definition
sections.summary: Notes the First Schedule restricts "platform services" to delivery and ride-hail services, and encourages continued engagement among Government, businesses and workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Although the Bill has been years in the making, it reflects Singapore’s ability, agility and responsiveness in adapting to the evolving needs of our workforce and business environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I commend the tripartite partners for their collaborative efforts in shaping a Bill that seeks to balance the interests of all stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As we move forward, I encourage continuous engagement among the Government, businesses and workers to ensure that the Bill remains adaptable to a rapidly changing landscape of the platform economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, I note that the First Schedule of the Bill restricts the definition of “platform services” to only delivery and ride-hail services.

sections.label: Other service workers not covered
sections.summary: States workers in these categories of services will not be covered by the Bill's protective measures today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Accordingly, workers in these categories of services will not be covered by the protective measures outlined in the Bill today.

sections.label: Threshold for regular human intervention
sections.summary: Asks what threshold defines human intervention as "regular or routine", removing a platform from the Bill's scope.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Government clarify what the threshold would be for human intervention that is considered to be “regular or routine”, such that this type of intervention would remove the platform concerned from the scope of the Bill?

sections.label: AWARE recommends gender-sensitive algorithms
sections.summary: AWARE recommends mandating that algorithms and rating systems be designed in a gender-sensitive way.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: AWARE recommends that it be mandated that algorithms and rating systems be designed in a gender-sensitive way.

sections.label: Arts self-employed workforce share
sections.summary: The Singapore Arts Plan states at least one-third of the arts workforce is self-employed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As I have mentioned previously in this House, and other Members have as well, in the arts, according to the latest Singapore Arts Plan, at least one-third of the workforce operates on a self-employed basis.

sections.label: Arts freelancer concerns and gaps
sections.summary: Arts freelancers face retirement worries, weak bargaining power, no Employment Act or WICA protection, costly disputes and limited insurance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Arts freelancers often worry about retirement adequacy, they have little to no bargaining power when negotiating contracts, they are not entitled to protection under the Employment Act and WICA, they have little recourse when contractual disputes occur because it can be costly and time-consuming to pursue legal action and they may not have access to work insurance coverage.

sections.label: New York Freelance Isn't Free Act
sections.summary: New York City's Freelance Isn't Free Act protects freelancers' rights to written contracts, timely full payment and against retaliation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In New York City, the “Freelance Isn’t Free Act” protects the entitlement of freelancers to written contracts, timely and full payment and provides protection from retaliation for individuals who exercise their rights under the law.

sections.label: Extending protection to arts freelancers
sections.summary: The Bill recognises some freelancers need legislative help, and asks if protection will extend to arts freelancers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The very Bill that we are debating today, recognises that certain types of freelancers do require legislative help in safeguarding their rights; and these are rights that we would normally see being protected only in traditional employer-employee relationships.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And so, my final clarification is this: would the Senior Minister of State consider extending legislative protection to more groups of freelancers in the future and in particular, to the arts community, which itself can also be quite a vulnerable group?

sections.label: Labour movement welcomes platform worker protections
sections.summary: The labour movement welcomes Manpower's initiative to strengthen platform worker protections through CPF contributions and WICA coverage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The labour movement warmly welcomes the Ministry of Manpower's initiative to strengthen protections for platform workers via the introduction of the CPF contributions and WICA coverage similar to employees.

sections.label: Offsetting platform worker CPF increases
sections.summary: The initiative offsets CPF contribution increases in 2025 and tapers off until 2029 so platform workers are not unduly burdened.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We must continue to refine our strategies and policies to ensure that the evolving needs of platform workers are met with the utmost fairness and efficiency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This initiative, set to fully offset the increase in CPF contributions to the Ordinary and Special Accounts in 2025 and, gradually taper off until 2029, is an important measure to ensure that these workers are not unduly burdened by the changes in CPF contribution requirements.

sections.label: WIS scheme disbursement changes
sections.summary: The Labour Movement welcomes enhancements to the WIS scheme, especially the shift from annual to monthly disbursements for eligible platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement also warmly welcomes enhancements to the WIS scheme, particularly the shift from annual to monthly disbursements for eligible platform workers.

sections.label: CPF contributions for platform workers
sections.summary: Platform workers who opt in will benefit from CPF contributions from platforms of up to 17% of their earnings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Platform workers who opt in this scheme will benefit from CPF contributions from platforms of up to 17% of their earnings.

sections.label: Government role in platform work
sections.summary: The Government has a crucial role in addressing challenges, with a more comprehensive strategy to improve career prospects of platform workers moving beyond gig work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The Government has a crucial role to play in addressing these challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: There should be a more comprehensive strategy aimed at improving the career prospects of platform workers who wish to move beyond gig work.

sections.label: Bill empowers platform workers
sections.summary: The Bill empowers platform workers to voice concerns about fairer payment terms, incentive-based policies, workplace health and safety, and fairer, more transparent penalty policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Some platform workers are still unsure, especially in relation to their working conditions and terms imposed by platform operators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: It is thus important that this Bill empowers platform workers to voice their concerns about fairer payment terms and incentive-based policies, their workplace health and safety, and fairer and more transparent penalty policies by platforms.

sections.label: NTUC support for platform workers
sections.summary: NTUC cares for platform workers, especially lower-wage roles, and believes encouraging younger workers to opt into CPF and enhancing job prospects through upskilling are crucial.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: NTUC deeply cares for our platform workers, especially those who are lower-wage roles, and is committed to make a tangible difference in their lives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We believe that encouraging younger workers to actively opt in into the CPF system, enhancing job prospects through targeted upskilling and career development programmes, are crucial steps in this process.

sections.label: Singapore tripartism works
sections.summary: Singapore's model of tripartism works to achieve progressive pro-worker outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Today, we are proof that Singapore's model of tripartism works to achieve progressive pro-worker outcomes.

sections.label: Platform workers bill basic needs
sections.summary: The Bill addresses platform workers' basic needs: work injury compensation, CPF contributions and a representative body.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Sometimes, as consumers, we might pay more attention on getting our orders fulfilled through the platform’s application, without thinking about the circumstances, fatigue and hardship experienced by platform workers who are also challenged by traffic or weather conditions, as well as the time pressure to fulfil the service.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill focuses specifically on the basic needs of platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It zooms in on compensation for work injuries in line with WICA standards, enhances their CPF contribution and provides for the establishment of a representative body for platform workers.

sections.label: Broad platform service definition
sections.summary: The First Schedule specifies delivery and ride-hail services, but the definitions cover other services not yet articulated.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, as also mentioned and similar to the points raised by hon Member prior, relating to the wide definition of the meaning of platform service, operator and the worker, I note that the First Schedule only specifies delivery and ride-hail services today.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, based on the meaning of platform service and platform operator, it does cover a broad definition that can be applied today to other types of services that may use similar platforms, but are not yet articulated in the First Schedule.

sections.label: Future services as platform work
sections.summary: It asks whether workers providing future platform-based services would also be considered platform workers under the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Is it envisioned, as technology further evolves, and more of such services can and will be delivered and made accessible through platform-based services, that the workers or professionals providing that specific service be considered as platform workers too under this Bill?

sections.label: CPF and regulatory cost concerns
sections.summary: Concerns are raised about CPF effects on platform workers' take-home pay, operators' costs and users' delivery charges.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For platform workers, there are concerns about how CPF contributions could impact, especially in the short to medium term, how much they will bring home each month in real terms to support their needs and their families.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For employers or platform operators, there are concerns about costs associated with the regulatory requirements from CPF contributions, WICA and the Workplace Safety and Health (WSH) Act.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, for users, at the last mile, it is also unclear how it will impact delivery charges and whether the availability of such services will be affected in the short term.

sections.label: Platform workers and company losses
sections.summary: Over 70,000 platform workers provide essential services, while Grab and Delivery Hero reported losses in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Today, over 70,000 platform workers in Singapore are working very hard every day to provide essential services and they deserve our support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: In 2023, last year, Grab reported a loss of $485 million and Delivery Hero, the parent company of Foodpanda, lost 2.3 billion euros.

sections.label: CPF offset for low-income workers
sections.summary: The Government will offset 100% of the 2025 CPF contribution increase for low-income platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The CPF contributions will help in their housing and retirement needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Thus, I applaud the Government's initiative to offset 100% of the increase in CPF contributions to the Ordinary and Special Accounts for low-income platform workers in 2025, making this transition smoother for those who need it most.

sections.label: Platform Workers Bill protection benefits
sections.summary: The Bill would protect 70,000 platform workers with CPF contributions, lower take-home pay, and workplace injury insurance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   If the Platform Workers Bill is passed, it will be a historic turning point, providing better protection for 70,000 platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Although platform workers' take-home pay will decrease, however, with the addition of CPF contributions from the platform operators, they will have more CPF funds to buy a home and accumulate more savings for retirement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Additionally, the Bill requires platform operators to purchase workplace injury compensation insurance for platform workers to better protect their interests if work-related injuries happen.

sections.label: WICA work injury compensation liability
sections.summary: The Ninth Schedule amends WICA 2019 to make platform operators liable for work injury compensation, benefiting food delivery workers lacking coverage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Fourthly, the Ninth Schedule amends the WICA 2019 to mandate platform operators' liability for work injury compensation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: This is particularly beneficial to food delivery workers, who currently lack insurance coverage.

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: The speaker firmly supports the Bill despite earlier clarifications and suggestions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Despite my above clarifications and suggestions, I firmly support the Bill.

sections.label: CPF alignment and injury insurance
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes aligning platform workers' CPF rates with employees and requiring injury insurance, but hopes the five-year period is shortened to three.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For example, in May 2021, I had requested the Ministry through a written Parliamentary Question to enact legislation to require companies hiring platform workers to recognise them as employees so that they can get the corresponding benefits and cover them for personal accident insurance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, I am delighted with the Ministry's decision to gradually align CPF contribution rates of platform workers with employees and require platform operators to purchase work injury compensation insurance for their platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   I do understand that the five-year period for the CPF changes is intended to help the platform operators and the platform workers adjust over time, but I hope that the Ministry would consider shortening this timeframe from five to three years.

sections.label: WIS eligibility and work hours
sections.summary: From 2029 eligible platform workers receive full employee WIS, and the speaker raises work hour limits not covered in the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: From 2029, all eligible platform workers will receive full employee WIS, up from the two-thirds of employees' WIS presently. : Next, I would like to raise an issue not covered in this Bill but which I hope can be included in a future amendment Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For normal employees, work cannot exceed 44 hours a week and total overtime cannot exceed 72 hours in a month.

sections.label: WSH Act safety duties
sections.summary: The Bill inserts section 12A into the WSH Act 2006, requiring platform operators to ensure worker safety and health.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: To address both safety and economic stability, I am pleased that the Bill includes legally binding duties for platform operators, specifically an insertion into the WSH Act 2006, section 12A.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: This requires platform operators to take necessary measures to ensure the safety and health of their workers, including measures to prevent exposing them to hazards arising from the platform operator's arrangements and processes.

sections.label: CPF mandatory savings for workers
sections.summary: The Bill ensures financial security for workers through mandatory savings via CPF.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Beyond safety, the Bill also ensures financial security for our workers through mandatory savings via CPF.

sections.label: Opting in above 30
sections.summary: The initiative aims to secure workers' future, and the speaker hopes more workers above 30 opt in.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: This initiative is a step towards securing their future and gifting them peace of mind in their later years.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: I sincerely hope more workers above 30 will choose to opt into the programme, for their long-term financial well-being.

sections.label: Tripartite approach and worker dignity
sections.summary: The Bill reflects a tripartite approach where Government, employers and unions work together, protecting livelihoods and securing workers' future.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: It also stands as a testament to our unique tripartite approach, where Government, employers, and unions work in concert to create balanced and effective policies.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: This Bill not only protects the livelihoods of our workers but also secures their future, offering them the dignity and peace of mind they deserve.

sections.label: Platform Workers Bill before House
sections.summary: The speaker recalls feeling something was unfair and is glad the Platform Workers Bill is before the House.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And I recall thinking that this does not feel fair, it does not feel right, and we got to change this somehow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Therefore, I am so glad that the Platform Workers Bill is finally before this House.

sections.label: Fixed Expense Deduction Amount
sections.summary: The Bill provides a Fixed Expense Deduction Amount, such as 20% for walkers, 35% for delivery riders and 60% for private hire vehicle drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Or take for example, the Fixed Expense Deduction Amount that this Bill provides for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Those elegant mathematical factors that crystallise the costs on a platform worker to perform platform work, so as to provide a simple and elegant way for everyone to determine net earnings from platform work – so, for example, 20% of earnings for a walker, 35% for a delivery rider on personal mobility device and 60% for a private hire vehicle driver in a car.

sections.label: Collective bargaining road ahead
sections.summary: The Bill empowers platform workers to engage in collective bargaining and deliberately avoids prescribing its scope.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Indeed, I would like to put to this House that beyond the challenges, and as much as arriving at this Bill is, in itself, a great leap forward for platform workers' rights and protection in Singapore, the centre of gravity of our efforts to advance and secure the rights and protection of platform workers, in their best interests will lie in the road ahead, and no less through the way in which we operationalise and realise the collective bargaining that this Bill will empower platform workers to engage in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: This Bill deliberately and wisely avoids making any prescription on the scope of this collective bargaining.

sections.label: Fair Pay for platform work
sections.summary: Proposes a Fair Pay principle that platform workers should be no worse off than local employees under the LQS Wage Schedule.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: First, I hope that we can forge a basic consensus, and crystallise and enshrine a basic principle, on what should constitute Fair Pay for platform work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And I like to suggest this principle: that a platform worker should be, on average, no worse off than a local employee receiving protection and assurance on wage floors under the Local Qualifying Scheme (LQS) Wage Schedule regime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: This means: (a) that a "full-time" platform worker, working up to 44 hours per week, should earn, on average, at least $1,600 a month net of all costs, on par with current LQS; (b) a "part-time" platform worker, working up to 35 hours per week, should earn, on average, at least $10.50 per hour, again net of costs; and (c) a "super garang" platform worker, pulling beyond 44 hours per week, and to hon Member Mr Gan Thiam Poh's point, should be remunerated for what is essentially "overtime", at a level that is, on average, at least on par with overtime pay as prescribed by the LQS Wage Schedule.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, for example, those platform workers who work 78 hours per week, or 11 hours per day for seven days of the week, should earn, on average, taking reference from the LQS Wage Schedule at least $2,000 net of all costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And if we apply the Fixed Expense Deduction Amount framework and gross up these net earnings for costs, this would translate to just over $16 an hour in gross takings – in other words, what a platform will pay the worker, for a delivery rider on a PMD doing food delivery as a side hustle, for example, or $5,000 a month in gross takings for a private hire vehicle driver who pulls 11 hours per day every day on the road.

sections.label: Tripartism and Platform Workers Bill
sections.summary: Says the Bill strengthens Singapore's tripartism and social compact, and that WP and PSP support it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And underpinning all these, it is about strengthening our unique model of tripartism in Singapore and strengthening our social compact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: I am hopeful that all stakeholders – platform workers, platform operators and consumers – will embrace the Platform Workers Bill in this spirit and forge ahead in the tough road of implementation ahead of us with that same spirit, to continue advancing and securing the rights and protection of platform workers in Singapore in the months and years ahead.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Both the WP and the PSP have spoken in support of this Bill to give platform workers better protection.

sections.label: Tripartite trust enables legislation
sections.summary: Singapore can enact this landmark legislation because of close working relationship and trust among tripartite partners.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Singapore is able to come up with this innovative and landmark piece of legislation because of the close working relationship and trust amongst the tripartite partners.

sections.label: PAP and NTUC symbiotic relationship
sections.summary: The symbiotic PAP-NTUC relationship lets the ruling party run a government both pro-worker and pro-business.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The symbiotic relationship of PAP and NTUC has allowed us, as the ruling party, to run a government that is both pro-worker and pro-business at the same time.

sections.label: WP accused of destroying tripartism
sections.summary: Says Singapore's tripartism exists because of PAP-NTUC mutual respect, and that WP leadership wants to destroy it.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The tripartism that we have in Singapore today, which many other countries want to emulate, only exists because of the close relationship and the mutual respect between the PAP and NTUC.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: So, all workers and employers should sit up and take notice because the WP leadership wants to destroy tripartism as it stands here today.

sections.label: Tripartism and PWAC recommendations
sections.summary: Says tripartism under the PAP Government is strong and the tripartite PWAC negotiated balanced recommendations now being legislated.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Fortunately, for Singapore, tripartism under the PAP Government is strong and, to NTUC and our unions, I say "Solidarity Forever".

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: And the Advisory Committee for Platform Workers (PWAC), which comprises tripartite representatives, was able to negotiate and come up with a balanced set of recommendations which we are now legislating through this Bill.

sections.label: Bill as social compact
sections.summary: The Bill being enacted is described as a declaration of the social compact.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The key thing is this: this Bill we are enacting today is a declaration of our social compact.

sections.label: Legislation for platform workers
sections.summary: The Government is enacting legislation to define platform workers as a distinct category of workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: It would have been far easier to just do nothing or perhaps take the easier approaches adopted elsewhere that unfortunately do not address the unique features of the platform workspace.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: This Government is taking the approach of enacting legislation to define platform workers as a distinct category of workers because we believe it is necessary and the right thing to do for this group of precarious workers.

sections.label: Balance of stakeholder interests
sections.summary: The Bill is a careful balance of stakeholder interests, protecting platform workers while keeping the platform economy sustainable.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: For example, to extend work injury compensation coverage to platform workers travelling to and from home or waiting for jobs; but this will further drive up the costs of protections that society will have to bear.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: I raise this observation to make the point that where we have landed at this Bill today is a careful balance of the interests of the various stakeholders involved to provide platform workers with the protection they need while making sure that the platform economy continues to be sustainable.

sections.label: Act supersedes less favourable contracts
sections.summary: When in force, obligations under the Act supersede existing contractual provisions that are less favourable.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: When the Bill comes into force, obligations on the platform operator or platform worker under the Act will supersede existing contractual provisions that are less favourable.

sections.label: Platform workers' total earnings increase
sections.summary: Platform workers will see an increase in total earnings after factoring in CPF contributions from platform operators.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Overall, platform workers will experience an increase in their total earnings after factoring in CPF contributions from the platform operators.

sections.label: PCTS income cap and budget
sections.summary: The qualifying income cap rose to $3,000 a month, and PCTS enhancements increased its estimated total budget by close to 60%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: As announced earlier, the qualifying income cap has been increased to $3,000 a month.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The median income of a platform worker ranges from $1,500 to $2,500 a month, so more than half of platform workers should meet the income criteria for the PCTS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: These enhancements to the PCTS have increased the estimated total budget for the PCTS by close to 60%.

sections.label: CPF for platform workers
sections.summary: Mandatory CPF contributions begin for platform workers born on or after 1995, respecting their autonomy while ensuring most eventually contribute.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Platform workers have given feedback that they prefer a choice to decide if they want to contribute CPF, based on their different needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Hence, we set the mandatory contribution for CPF to begin for those who are born on or after 1995.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: It respects the autonomy of the platform workers while ensuring that on a cohort basis over time, a majority of platform workers will have mandatory CPF contributions.

sections.label: CPF rates for older workers
sections.summary: The Government remains committed to the 2019 Tripartite Workgroup recommendation to align CPF contribution rates for employees aged above 55 to 60 with those 55 and below.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Mr Ang will be pleased to know that we remain committed to implementing the 2019 recommendation by the Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers to align the CPF contribution rates for employees aged above 55 to 60 to those of employees aged 55 and below.

sections.label: Road user fatality rates
sections.summary: Fatality rates are 20% for walking, 35% for riding a motorbike and 60% for driving.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: As you heard from Mr Xie Yao Quan's speech earlier, 20% if you are walking, 35% if you are riding a motorbike, 60% if you are driving.

sections.label: Work injury insurance insurers
sections.summary: The new work injury compensation insurance market will be led by insurers from the Platform Workers Work Injury Compensation Implementation Network as first-movers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The new work injury compensation insurance market will be led by insurers from the Platform Workers Work Injury Compensation Implementation Network as first-movers.

sections.label: Appointing insurer for claims
sections.summary: Where multiple platform operators are liable, MOM will appoint one operator's insurer to process the claim for timely payouts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: If multiple platform operators are liable, MOM will appoint the insurer of one of those platform operators to process the claim for timely payouts to the platform worker.

sections.label: Platform work safety code
sections.summary: Platform operators must review and address safety and health risks, put into practice through the Approved Code of Practice for Platform Services being consulted on.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Platform operators need to review and address the safety and health risks arising from platform work, as with companies in other industries.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: This will be put into practice through the Approved Code of Practice for Platform Services, which MOM and the WSH Council are consulting the public on.

sections.label: MOM electronic voting for ballots
sections.summary: MOM will conduct electronic voting for secret ballots for recognition.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: MOM will conduct electronic voting for secret ballots for recognition.

sections.label: Platform worker earning slips
sections.summary: MPs suggested minimum earnings for platform workers; the law will require platform operators to provide earning slips stating workers are platform workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Mr Xie Yao Quan, Mr Louis Chua and Mr Leong Mun Wai had various suggestions on introducing minimum earnings for platform workers as well.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We agree that the law should set basic standards on platform work in terms of transparency.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: For example, we will require platform operators to keep records of and provide their workers with earning slips.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: These earning slips must also state that they are for platform workers, so that platform workers know that they are platform workers and are aware of their rights.

sections.label: Risks of overregulation
sections.summary: On calls for more regulatory requirements and minimum earnings, the risks of impractical and counter-productive overregulation should be noted.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: On the broader points made by the various MPs asking for more regulatory requirements and minimum earnings, we should be mindful of the risks of overregulation that is impractical and counter-productive.

sections.label: Clause 6(1)(b) intent
sections.summary: Clause 6(1)(b) of the Bill intends to capture entities where automation of data use for a specified purpose is the primary mode of operation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Put another way, the intent of clause 6(1)(b) of the Bill is to capture entities where automation of the use of data for a specified purpose is the primary mode of operation.

sections.label: Transition support and insurance premiums
sections.summary: The Government provided transition support through the PCTS and will monitor work injury compensation insurance premiums, with consumers also having a role.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The Government has provided generous transition support through the PCTS and will monitor work injury compensation insurance premiums.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Consumers, too, will have a role to play.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: I should emphasise that the costs arising from providing platform workers with basic protections are no different in nature from the business costs that other employers are already incurring to provide CPF and work injury compensation to their employees today.

sections.label: Auditing platform operator costs
sections.summary: The costs incurred by platform operators on work injury compensation and CPF can also be audited.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The costs incurred by platform operators on work injury compensation and CPF can also be audited.

sections.label: Platform worker training allowance
sections.summary: From early 2025, platform workers above 40 can use the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Training Allowance for eligible full-time training, but not the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: From early-2025 onwards, platform workers above 40 years of age can also tap on the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Training Allowance to pursue eligible full-time training programmes, such as the full-time SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme to support mid-career transitions into sectors with good employment opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: They will receive a monthly training allowance computed as 50% of their average monthly income and capped at $3,000 a month, over a lifetime cap of 24 months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: However, the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support scheme will not be open to platform workers, to answer Ms Pereira's question.

sections.label: Platform workers legislation benefits
sections.summary: The legislation will let platform workers benefit from improved housing and retirement adequacy, work injury compensation coverage and representation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The result is a legislation that will allow platform workers to benefit from improved housing and retirement adequacy, coverage for work injury compensation and representation.

sections.label: Untethering NTUC from PAP
sections.summary: The call is for a key reform to untether the NTUC from the PAP and free unionists to be independent advocates for workers in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What we are calling for is a key reform to untether the NTUC from the PAP and free up unionists to be independent advocates for workers in Singapore.

sections.label: PAP and NTUC equal partnership
sections.summary: The relationship between PAP and NTUC is an equal partnership, and union leaders are elected by workers, not a subordinate relationship.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: The first point I want to say is that the relationship between PAP and NTUC – the symbolic relationship – is an equal partnership.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Our union leaders are elected by the workers to represent them.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: It is not a subordinate relationship between PAP and NTUC.

sections.label: Unionists independent advocacy quote
sections.summary: A quoted unionist says NTUC-affiliated unionists have never flinched from raising concerns and advocating for members' rights, wages, prospects and welfare.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: And he went on to say that, "as unionists of unions affiliated with NTUC Singapore, we have never flinched from raising our concerns and advocating for our members' rights for better wages and for better work prospects and welfare.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: It would be foolhardy to think that unionists are not independent." So, please have a care, give some respect to our unionists and union leaders on the ground.

sections.label: NTUC pushing unaccepted policies
sections.summary: NTUC has pushed for many policies the Government has not accepted over the years, and will continue to do so, with the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support scheme as an example.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: On the Member's questions about whether we have policies where we have differed from what the Government suggests, I would gladly say that NTUC has been pushing for many policies that, even over the years, the Government has not accepted, but we will continue to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: The SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support scheme is one very good example.

sections.label: Convention C87 ratification and unions
sections.summary: Singapore does not ratify Convention C87 because it requires registration of unions, and the US and New Zealand have also not ratified it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: That is the nature of it, but we will never flinch and we will never refrain ourselves from speaking up or have any fear or favour when doing so.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We do not ratify Convention C87 because we require registration of unions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The tripartite relationship is built on trust so that there is trust between the tripartite partners involved in negotiations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: And just so that the Member is aware, there are actually quite a number of countries that have ratified, but it might also be useful for the Member to know that countries like the US and New Zealand have also not ratified this particular convention that the Member raised.

sections.label: WP rejects Koh Poh Koon comments
sections.summary: The Worker's Party rejects Senior Minister of State Koh Poh Koon's comments and his characterisation of harmonious industrial relations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One, I reject, and the WP will reject, Senior Minister of State Koh Poh Koon's comments on the WP entirely and his characterisation of harmonious industrial relations between workers, employers and the government of the day as being something the WP does not agree with.

sections.label: CPF opt-in versus opt-out
sections.summary: The speaker questions whether administrative costs justify not defaulting to opt-out for platform workers' CPF, noting CPF LIFE already defaults to opt-out.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Senior Minister of State Koh, if I heard correctly, indicated that the reasons for not defaulting to an opt-out rather than an opt-in approach for the CPF system was due to extra administrative costs that will be borne by the Government as well as platform companies and also the possibility of a diminished choice.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If what I did hear was true, I find this puzzling because after all, there is certainly no loss of choice either from opting out or opting in, that is the nature of opting.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And there are indeed already Government schemes, pension schemes, such as CPF LIFE, where opting out is the default.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: More generally, I suppose, what I should be asking is: are we allowing the possibility of some additional administrative costs to be the basis for us not ensuring that the retirement adequacy of our platform workers is actually made more secure?

sections.label: Reasons for opt-in CPF system
sections.summary: An opt-in system with no later opting out was chosen for administrative ease and simplicity, as operators and workers desired.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Whereas, if you let people decide that they want to come in, then the operator only needs to do it one time and process the onboarding cost for that worker coming onto the system.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: That is why in our construct, we disallow people from opting out thereafter, once they opt in, so that the operator only does one time of onboarding and does not have to keep flipflopping workers in and out.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Opting out as a default is also a challenge because some workers may then choose to be out of one operator but not the other, and it becomes very messy for the operators to track whether this worker is on which system.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, I think for administrative ease and for simplicity of operating a very complex system with many combinations of worker preferences to begin with, we have decided, together with the operators and also the desire of the workers, to go for an opt-in system.

sections.label: Scope of platform work negotiation
sections.summary: Platform work associations and operators decide the scope of negotiation, including base fees, rather than one-size-fits-all regulation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Whether there can be, for example, a base fee, that is something that the operators have to decide on whether that is something financially viable for them to do.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We leave it to the platform work associations and operators to decide on the scope of negotiation, because it can differ from platform to platform.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Some platforms may be prepared to offer that but, for other platforms, their business model and the cost structure may not allow that to happen.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, I think rather than have a one-size-fits-all regulation, we allow representation to take place so that from an association to an individual operator's business model basis, they can scope out what works best for them and decide even on the scope that they are prepared to discuss.

sections.label: Guarding against cost pass-through
sections.summary: Keeping the sector competitive is important to guard against excessive cost increases or profiteering from cost pass-through.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: On the first question of cost transfer or pass-through to stakeholders, the thing that we think would be important to guard against any excessive cost increase or profiteering would be to make sure that the sector continues to remain competitive.

sections.label: WICA costs for platform workers
sections.summary: Insurers estimate WICA costs for platform workers will not be much higher than current WICA costs for logistics or transport drivers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: On the WICA costs, based on our engagement with insurers through the Platform Workers Work Injury Compensation Network, where we work with five or seven insurers to start with, their estimate is that the cost of WICA for platform workers will not be too much higher compared to the current WICA costs for drivers in the logistics or transport sector, for example.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: It may be slightly higher because, today, there is no actuarial data, so everyone is pricing a little bit more conservatively.

sections.label: Market time for WICA equilibrium
sections.summary: The market should be given time to reach equilibrium, with insurers sensing costs will not be excessively higher than current WICA for the same sector.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, I think we should probably give the market some time to come to an equilibrium.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But the initial sensing from the insurers is that it will not be excessively much higher, compared to what WICA is today for employees of the same sector.

sections.label: NTUC subordinate to PAP claim
sections.summary: The suggestion that NTUC is subordinate to PAP interests in Labour Movement negotiations is completely inaccurate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Point number two about Mr Gerald Giam's insinuations, that there is a suggestion that NTUC is subordinate to the PAP's interests when it comes to Labour Movement negotiations and trajectories, this is completely inaccurate.

sections.label: NTUC and PAP separate organisations
sections.summary: Tether or untether means NTUC and PAP should be separate, independent organisations not pledging symbiosis to each other.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: When I say "tether" or "untether", what I mean is that NTUC and PAP should be separate, independent organisations and should not be pledging symbiosis to each other – that is all I mean.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: And what he says about it not being a subordinate relationship, can I ask the Member why is there then a need for the platform work associations to have a council of advisors which has the power to dismiss the executive council?

sections.label: Tripartism as Singapore's formula
sections.summary: The Member is asked not to unravel Singapore's good tripartism formula between Government, employers and employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: My answer to the hon Member Mr Giam is that, please, do not seek to unravel a secret formula, a good formula that we have in Singapore which is tripartism between the Government, the employers and the employees.

sections.label: NTUC and Government relationship
sections.summary: The relationship between NTUC and the Government is more than what is seen in the world today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: However, I think the issue here that we are trying to push, trying to clarify or trying to stress, is that the nature of the relationship between the NTUC and our Government is more than what we have seen in the world today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: It is more than what we see in the world today, for example, what I am trying to say is, can you find another trade union in the world where the trade union chief is a Minister.

sections.label: Unions negotiating wage cuts, SERS
sections.summary: Unions worked with SNEF to negotiate wage cuts and save jobs, and NTUC administered the Self-employed Persons Income Relief Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Our unions worked collectively with SNEF to share the burden, negotiating wage cuts, saving jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: And the unions, NTUC, even administered the Self-employed Persons Income Relief Scheme, or SERS.

sections.label: SNEF on unions without strikes
sections.summary: SNEF's view was that unions here are strong because they get what they want without striking.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: SNEF's view, his response to this foreign counterpart's comment was, actually, no, the unions here are strong because they get what they want without striking.

sections.label: Clause 13 insurance amendments
sections.summary: Amendments to clause 13 are required for consistency across sections 31(a) and 31(1b) of the Work Injury Compensation Act.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The amendments to clause 13 are required for the consistency across section 31(a) and section 31(1b) of the Work Injury Compensation Act to require both a designated employer's insurer and a designated platform operator's insurer to provide insurance.

sections.label: Platform worker numbers and earnings
sections.summary: As of 2023, around 70,000 platform workers make up about 3% of the workforce, with median earnings of $1,500 to $2,500 a month.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: As of 2023, there are around 70,000 platform workers, comprising about 3% of our workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: In 2023, their median earnings were around $1,500 to $2,500 a month.

sections.label: Government accepts PWAC recommendations
sections.summary: In November 2022, after a year-long PWAC process, the Government accepted the PWAC's recommendations, which the Platform Workers Bill gives effect to.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: In November 2022, following a year-long process of engagements and deliberations by the PWAC, the Government accepted the PWAC's recommendations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: This Platform Workers Bill today will give effect to these recommendations.

sections.label: Legislation for upfront clarity
sections.summary: The Government decided to provide clarity upfront through legislation while preserving flexibility for workers and companies in platform work.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: The downside of this approach is a lack of clarity for both the workers and companies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: We have decided that it is better for the Government to provide clarity upfront for companies and workers through legislation and to do so in a way that preserves the flexibility that both workers and companies wish to retain for platform work.

sections.label: Platform worker definition and protections
sections.summary: Clause 5 defines platform workers as a middle category between employees and self-employed, with statutory protections for a distinct group.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Clause 5 of the Bill defines platform workers as individuals who have contracts with and are subject to the management control of a platform operator in their provision of services, but who are not employees of the platform operator, in effect, creating a middle category of workers in between employees and self-employed persons.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Singapore is among the first in the world to take this approach of providing statutory protections for platform workers as a distinct group.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: If the Bill is passed, companies that meet the definition of platform operator must comply with their statutory obligations and provide protections to their platform workers once the Bill comes into effect.

sections.label: CPF contribution rates 2025
sections.summary: From 2025, platform operators contribute 3.5% of net earnings and platform workers contribute up to 2.5% more.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Starting in 2025, platform operators will contribute 3.5% of platform workers' net earnings and platform workers will contribute up to an additional 2.5%.

sections.label: PCTS offset enhancement
sections.summary: The PCTS offset, announced in 2023 at 75% then 50%, will be enhanced to offset 100% of the increase in 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: We had previously announced in 2023 that the PCTS would offset 75% of platform workers' increase in CPF contributions in the first year and 50% in the second year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: We will enhance this to offset 100% of the increase in 2025.

sections.label: Employee-level Workfare from 2029
sections.summary: From 2029, platform workers contributing CPF like employees receive employee-level Workfare, up to $4,900 yearly, 40% in cash.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: In addition, from 2029 onwards, platform workers who contribute CPF at the same rate now, by then, like an employee, will receive employee-level Workfare, instead of just two-thirds the amount like self-employed persons.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: This means that they will benefit from higher Workfare payments of up to $4,900 a year, with a higher proportion paid in cash – 40% instead of the 10%, like a self-employed person.

sections.label: CPF computation with FEDA
sections.summary: CPF for platform workers is computed on earnings less a Fixed Expense Deduction Amount, or FEDA, due to unreimbursed work expenses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: However, unlike employees, platform workers incur work expenses which are not reimbursed, such as fuel cost.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Hence, the computation of CPF for platform workers will be based on earnings, less a Fixed Expense Deduction Amount, or FEDA.

sections.label: Platform operators pay CPF monthly
sections.summary: Platform operators must pay both the platform operator and platform worker share of CPF contribution to the CPF Board monthly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Like in the employer-employee model, the onus is on platform operators to pay both the platform operator and platform worker share of CPF contribution to the CPF Board monthly.

sections.label: CPF reimbursement for parental leave
sections.summary: The Government will reimburse platform operators' CPF contribution share, on top of lost income, when platform workers seek parental leave reimbursement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: They are not getting CPF contributions from the operator to begin with.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: But moving forward, for platform workers who are mandated or have opted-in to boost their CPF savings, the Government will also reimburse the platform operators' share of CPF contribution, on top of their lost income, when platform workers seek reimbursement for parental leave.

sections.label: Work injury compensation coverage
sections.summary: Amended Act requires platform operators to give work injury compensation at employee-level coverage, including medical expenses, income loss and lump sum compensation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Under the amended Act, platform operators will be required to provide work injury compensation to platform workers at the same level of coverage, as employees, comprising reimbursement for medical expenses, income loss compensation for medical leave and hospitalisation leave and a lump sum compensation for permanent incapacity or death.

sections.label: Illegal vehicle and licensing exclusions
sections.summary: Platform workers are not eligible for work injury compensation for injuries from illegally modified vehicles or if unlicensed to operate the vehicle.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: As platform workers have the autonomy to choose the vehicle used to perform platform work, under the amended WICA, platform workers will not be eligible for work injury compensation if the injury was caused by their use of an illegally modified vehicle, or if the platform worker was not licensed to operate the vehicle in the first place.

sections.label: Eligibility during pick-up and delivery
sections.summary: Platform workers will be eligible for work injury compensation when performing pick-up and delivery of passengers or goods.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Platform workers will be eligible for work injury compensation when they are performing pick-up and delivery of passengers or goods.

sections.label: Liability of one platform operator
sections.summary: For platform workers injured while performing a job for one platform operator, that platform operator will be liable.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: With reference to paragraph 17 of the Ninth Schedule of the Bill, for platform workers injured while performing a job for one platform operator, that platform operator will be liable.

sections.label: Apportioning liability between operators
sections.summary: For delivery work for two platform operators, compensation liability is apportioned based on earnings with each operator over the past 90 days.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: If the platform worker was performing "delivery" for two platform operators A and B, compensation liability will be apportioned among both platform operators based on the platform worker's earnings with each platform operator over the past 90 days on lookback.

sections.label: Platform work associations legal framework
sections.summary: Associations champion platform workers' interests, but no legal framework exists for their representation, so tripartite partners agree a legal framework is needed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: For platform work, the National Private Hire Vehicles Association, the National Taxi Association and the National Delivery Champions Association have been actively working to understand the challenges that platform workers in the ride-hail and delivery sectors face, and champion their interests.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: However, as platform workers are not employees, there is currently no legal framework for the representation of platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
