sentences.text: While there has been constructive dialogue between the associations and platform operators, tripartite partners agree that the process can be strengthened through a legal framework that sets out the rights and obligations of both platform work associations and platform operators in dealing with each other.

sections.label: Secret ballot for industrial action
sections.summary: Clause 36(1) requires a platform work association to obtain majority consent by secret ballot before organising or commencing industrial action.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: As such, under clause 36(1) of the Bill, a platform work association must not organise or commence industrial action if it has not obtained the consent, by secret ballot, of the majority of members affected by the industrial action.

sections.label: CPF increase and opt-in
sections.summary: CPF contribution increases will be paced over five years, and older platform workers may opt in to higher CPF contributions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: For CPF, we will pace the increase in CPF contribution over five years and give older platform workers the choice to opt in to higher CPF contributions.

sections.label: Protections for platform workers
sections.summary: The Government will strengthen protections in housing and retirement adequacy, work injury compensation, and representation, gradually raising CPF contribution rates over five years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: However, platform work is precarious, so the Government will strengthen protections for platform workers in three areas: first, housing and retirement adequacy; second, work injury compensation and; third, allowing platform work associations to represent platform workers and safeguard their interests.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We will gradually increase the CPF contribution rates for platform operators and workers over five years, in order to reduce the impact on platform operators and workers.

sections.label: PCTS covers 2025 CPF contributions
sections.summary: The Government has enhanced the Platform Workers' CPF Transition Support to fully cover platform workers' additional CPF contributions in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The Government has enhanced the Platform Workers' CPF Transition Support (PCTS), to fully cover the additional CPF contributions required from the platform workers in 2025.

sections.label: PCTS income ceiling raised
sections.summary: The monthly income ceiling for PCTS has been raised from $2,500 to $3,000, benefitting more platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: At the same time, the monthly income ceiling for PCTS has been raised from $2,500 to $3,000, thus benefitting more platform workers.

sections.label: Platform work associations and Bill timeline
sections.summary: Platform work associations can negotiate with stakeholders, and the Bill is planned to take effect from 1 January 2025.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Platform work associations will be able to communicate and negotiate with stakeholders, such as platform operators and mall operators, to better address the issues and challenges faced by platform workers. : If the Bill is passed, we plan for the Bill to take effect from 1 January 2025 as the intention is to allow platform workers to benefit from the protections as soon as possible, while bringing more convenience to platform operators and platform workers by having the increased CPF contribution rates and tax relief computed from the start of the calendar year.

sections.label: Platform workers in labour force
sections.summary: In 2023, there were 70,500 platform workers, forming 2.9% of the labour force.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2023, there were 70,500 platform workers who formed 2.9% of the labour force.

sections.label: Median income of platform occupations
sections.summary: MOM reported the median gross monthly income of full-time platform-related occupations was $2,000 in 2023, unchanged from 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: MOM reported that the median gross monthly income of full-time platform-related occupations was $2,000 in 2023, unchanged from 2022.

sections.label: Platform workers' savings decline
sections.summary: Platform workers' savings fell to 1.7 months' worth of expenses in May 2023, compared to 1.9 months a year before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Arising from this, the savings of platform workers fell to 1.7 months' worth of expenses in May 2023, compared to 1.9 months a year before.

sections.label: Workers' Party supports Bill
sections.summary: The Workers' Party supports the Bill as it seeks regulatory changes to better serve platform workers' interests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For these reasons, the Workers' Party (WP) supports this Bill, as it seeks to advance regulatory changes that will ultimately better-serve the interests of platform workers.

sections.label: MediSave contributions by platform workers
sections.summary: It was assessed that only about 45% of platform workers made some contribution to their MediSave accounts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While the Senior Minister of State did not have the data on hand, it was assessed that only about 45% of platform workers made some contribution to their MediSave accounts.

sections.label: Median age of platform workers
sections.summary: 2023 MOM data shows resident regular primary platform workers had a median age in the mid-50s, with only 8.4% aged 30 and below.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Thirdly, based on 2023 MOM data, the median age of resident regular primary platform workers was in the mid-50s.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Only 8.4% of such workers were aged 30 and below – 8.4%.

sections.label: Platform workers aged 30 to 49
sections.summary: Platform workers aged 30 to 39 form 10.8% of the total and those aged 40 to 49 form 18.8%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Platform workers aged 30 to 39 form 10.8% of the total and those aged 40 to 49% form 18.8% of the total.

sections.label: CPF contribution rates under Bill
sections.summary: Under the Bill, CPF contribution rates rise yearly until reaching 20% from workers and 17% from platforms, with Government contributing 75% in the first year, reducing to 25% in 2027, and fully offsetting 2025 contributions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Fifthly, under the Bill, the CPF contribution rates for workers and platforms would be increased by a few percentage points each year, until it reaches 20% from platform workers and 17% from platforms later in this decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government would contribute 75% of the workers' contribution in the first year and this would reduce to 25% in 2027.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A few weeks ago, the Government announced that it would totally offset the first contribution for the year 2025 by 100%, thus subsidising the workers' entire CPF contribution next year.

sections.label: WICA cost awareness for platforms
sections.summary: With WICA implementation three months away, the question asks whether platform companies know its cost to be ready by 1 January 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With the implementation date for WICA for platform workers a mere three months away, are platform companies aware of how much WICA will cost them, so as to be ready to roll out coverage for platform workers by 1 January 2025?

sections.label: WICA needed for consistent protection
sections.summary: Grab provides prolonged medical leave insurance, but the varied platform space and coverage mean WICA is necessary for better, consistent basic protection for vulnerable workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Grab has been providing drivers and delivery partners prolonged medical leave insurance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, the varied nature of the platform space and, by extension, the varied and different coverage for work injuries suffered by our workers, means that WICA is necessary to ensure better and consistent basic protection for our most vulnerable workers.

sections.label: Incentives, representation and Bill success
sections.summary: Incentives may encourage representation, a survey found 55% of food delivery workers unwilling to pay representation fees, and the Bill's success depends on reasonable price rises, equitable distribution and shared responsibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This may be an important incentive to get platform workers to seek better representation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Such incentives are needed, given that a survey carried out by Grab, Deliveroo and Foodpanda revealed that 55% of food delivery workers said they are unwilling to pay any fees for representation, suggesting a lack of understanding at what representation can offer or a lack of belief of how representation can benefit them in concrete terms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To conclude, Sir, the success of this Bill for the Singaporean public will turn on how reasonable the anticipated price rises of platform services will be after the Bill becomes law and whether the increase is equitably distributed between consumers, platforms and workers – bearing in mind that nothing stops any company or service provider from capitalising on significant regulatory changes to profiteer or socialise costs more than it should.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While the Bill represents an improvement in social security and fairer working conditions for our platform workers, its effectiveness hinges on resolving ambiguities and the acceptance of important social responsibilities by not just platform companies and consumers, but platform workers accepting some responsibility for their own security too.

sections.label: Platform worker protections bill
sections.summary: The Bill proposes mandatory CPF contributions, insurance coverage and formal representation for over 75,000 platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: On one hand, it provides our platform workers with the basic protections they deserve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This is a significant win for the more than 75,000 platform workers, who rely on this work for their livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: For too long, these workers have operated in the grey area, unable to benefit from the protections of the Employment Act and relying on the goodwill of platform companies for insurance coverage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This Bill proposes to provide them with a safety net through mandatory CPF contributions, insurance coverage and the right to formal representation.

sections.label: Work injury compensation for riders
sections.summary: The Bill introduces mandatory work injury compensation for platform workers, giving them the same WICA protection as traditional employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: A 2022 survey by the Institute of Policy Studies, further underscores the urgency of this issue, finding that more than a third of delivery riders in Singapore had been in some forms of accident requiring medical attention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Yet without legislative protection, they are left with the financial brunt of such incidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This Bill will introduce mandatory work injury compensation for platform workers, providing them with the same level of protection as traditional employees under WICA.

sections.label: Associations protecting platform workers
sections.summary: The Bill empowers associations to protect platform workers' rights from the outset, preventing delayed access to basic protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The absence of formal representation delayed their access to basic protection for years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This Bill seeks to prevent such struggles by empowering associations to protect platform workers' rights from the outset.

sections.label: Guidelines and arbitration system
sections.summary: The question asks how the Ministry ensures clear guidelines and a robust arbitration system so payouts are not unduly delayed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: To address this, how does the Ministry ensure guidelines are sufficiently clear and robust and there will be a robust arbitration system in place so that the payouts are not unduly delayed?

sections.label: Focus on transport and delivery
sections.summary: The question asks the Ministry to clarify its rationale for focusing on transportation and delivery services and whether a periodic review mechanism exists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry clarify its rationale for focusing on transportation and delivery services now?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: And will there be a periodic review mechanism to update the definition of "platform workers" as the gig economy evolves?

sections.label: Gig economy and landmark Bill
sections.summary: The Bill recognises gig platform workers as being in employee-like arrangements, allowing union-like representation and workplace injury insurance, retirement and housing adequacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In recent years, the rise of digital platforms alongside the proliferation of smartphones and the mobile Internet led to the emergence of a different class of own account workers: those who may not entirely be in control of their own business, such as private hire car drivers and food delivery riders, working for the ubiquitous multi-billion dollar platform companies we see today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While the gig economy is often hailed for its flexibility and autonomy, the reality is that with ever-increasing app sophistication and as these platforms grow in scale, the gig economy has evolved in ways that increasingly disadvantage its workers, and such work is often arduous, risky and poorly remunerated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Behind the appeal of flexibility and the promise of independence lies a reality fraught with inadequate protections and financial insecurity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: NTUC and our affiliate associations – the National Taxi Association, National Private Hire Vehicles Association and National Delivery Champions Association have worked for years on advocating and planning for this debate today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This landmark Bill, if passed into law, recognises that self-employed gig platform workers are in employee-like work arrangements with platform operators and will allow platform workers, such as our taxi and private hire vehicle drivers and delivery riders, to be formally represented by union-like associations under Singapore's labour laws, and to be accorded, rightfully, fair and even workplace injury insurance, as well as retirement and housing adequacy, alongside all Singaporean employees.

sections.label: MediSave matching for drivers
sections.summary: In 2010 the National Taxi Association advocated taxi companies matching MediSave contributions for drivers under "Drive and Save", replicated in 2017 by the National Private Hire Vehicles Association with Grab.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In 2010, the National Taxi Association advocated for taxi companies to match MediSave Contributions for our drivers under the "Drive and Save" scheme, and the National Private Hire Vehicles Association replicated this successfully for our private hire vehicle drivers in 2017 with Grab.

sections.label: Workgroup on delivery rider conditions
sections.summary: Earlier this year NTUC mooted and co-led a multi-agency workgroup with Government, condominium MCSTs and mall operators to look into delivery riders' work and safety conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, NTUC mooted for and co-led a multi-agency workgroup comprising the Government and private sector condominium Management Corporation Strata Titles and mall operators to look into work and safety conditions for our delivery riders.

sections.label: Peak-hour shifts earnings
sections.summary: By targeting peak-hour shifts he earned a steady $2,500 a month, supporting himself and taking on long-term financial commitments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: By targeting peak-hour shifts, he was able to earn a comfortable steady $2,500 a month, and this allowed him the ability to support himself and to take on some long-term financial commitments.

sections.label: Mandating WICA-like work injury insurance
sections.summary: The speaker says work injury insurance is not a game and supports mandating WICA-like coverage for platform workers, covering all workers at all times regardless of targets, transport mode, activity level or ranking.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: But what happens to the families left behind?

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, Mr Speaker, I put it to you that work injury insurance not a game, 工伤赔偿不可能当成游戏, and I support the mandating of a WICA-like coverage for our platform workers, akin to that enjoyed by the rest of the Singaporean employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Work injury insurance should not be tied to whether a worker meets performance targets or has a specific mode of transport.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Insurance must cover all workers, at all times, regardless of their activity level or their ranking within a system.

sections.label: Platform operators' CPF share
sections.summary: The question asks how the Ministry would ensure platform operators pay their fair share of platform workers' CPF, keeping in mind operators need to be sustainable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: How would the Ministry ensure that our platform operators pay for their fair share of their platform workers’ CPF, keeping in mind that platform operators need to be sustainable also?

sections.label: Fair CPF and insurance contributions
sections.summary: The question asks how to ensure platforms contribute fairly to CPF and insurance without passing costs to workers and consumers, and whether MOM would require fare breakdowns stating CPF shares.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Given that we agree that platform workers are treated as employee-like, how do we ensure that platforms contribute fairly to CPF and insurance without passing the costs onto workers and end consumers through reduced pay or higher fees?

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Would MOM be requiring platform companies to provide clear breakdown of fares to both workers and end consumers stating clearly their share of CPF contributions?

sections.label: PCTS extension and CPF for platform workers
sections.summary: Asks whether the PCTS scheme can be extended to drivers earning more than $2,500, and says platform operators should pay CPF for platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Given that anecdotally, from our drivers and riders' feedback that real earnings have gone down and drivers need to drive longer hours, can we also extend the PCTS scheme for all drivers even those who earn more than $2,500 today?

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As employee-like workers, platform workers' retirement and housing adequacy worries must be addressed, by having platform operators pay for their fair share of CPF.

sections.label: Global growth of platform economy
sections.summary: Estimates suggest it will grow from $12 trillion to $17 trillion worldwide by 2028, accounting for almost a fifth of global output.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Estimates suggest that by 2028, it will grow from the current $12 trillion to $17 trillion worldwide, accounting for almost a fifth of all global output.

sections.label: Platform firms outperform old-school firms
sections.summary: A study found the largest platform companies produced twice the growth, profits and market capitalisation of the largest old-school firms in the same business, with half the workers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A recent study established that the largest platform companies have been able to churn out twice the growth, profits and market capitalisation than the largest old-school firms operating in the same business, all while doing so with half the number of workers.

sections.label: Platform worker classification and labour protections
sections.summary: Part 1 of the Bill creates a new classification of platform workers to extend labour protections, and the speaker hopes the First Schedule will eventually cover crowdworkers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The new classification of platform workers that will result from Part 1 of the Bill helps ensure that workers in this intermediate no-man's land will be extended proper labour protections.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is already somewhat belated, with jurisdictions such as the UK having recognised so-called "limb (b)" workers in 2021 and the state of California having extended full employee classification to platform workers in 2019, although that has recently been overturned.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But better late than never, although I would hope that the Bill should also consider eventually extending the coverage of the First Schedule to another category of platform workers: those who contribute towards and are paid for their part in a crowdsourced task – otherwise known as crowdworkers.

sections.label: WP support for PCTS and opt-out
sections.summary: The WP supports the Bill's stipulations encouraging enrolment, welcomes the enhanced PCTS in the Fifth Schedule, and notes Pritam Singh suggested an opt-out rather than opt-in regime.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Consequently, the WP is in favour of the stipulations in the Bill that will encourage such workers to enrol with the system.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The proposed enhanced PCTS embedded into the Fifth Schedule certainly offers a welcome alternative to encourage participation in the higher-contribution Group A, at least up till 2028.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Leader of the Opposition Pritam Singh has further suggested that the default be set as an opt-out rather than an opt-in regime.

sections.label: Platform workers below age 30
sections.summary: Only around 7% of platform workers are below 30 years of age.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Only a fraction of around 7% of platform workers are indeed below 30 years of age.

sections.label: Platform worker earnings reporting
sections.summary: Government should work with platform providers to ensure accurate earnings reporting, facilitating CPF submissions and retirement planning, with independent audits.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For platform workers that do enrol as Group A workers, it would be useful for the Government to work with platform providers themselves to ensure the accurate reporting of earnings in much the same manner that employers are currently obliged to accurately declare salary information for wage-earning employees.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This would facilitate retirement planning and submissions to CPF, but it may call for some automated transfer of aggregated monthly earnings data since platform workers' earnings are transactions-based.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: These data should, of course, also be open to audit, ideally by a truly independent third party.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While I support the enhanced protections being made available to them, I, like my WP colleagues, caution against an excessively sanguine attitude to platform providers, to the detriment of our hardworking gig workers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We must make gig work work for their retirement.

sections.label: Platform worker protection and CPF
sections.summary: Platform workers may need protection from threats, abuse and unfair reviews, and will receive matching CPF contributions based on earnings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We may need to look into provisions for platform workers to be protected from threats, abuse and unfair reviews given by unreasonable customers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am most assured that platform workers will receive matching CPF contributions based on the amounts they earn, whether they work for a single or multiple platforms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This will help them move towards better housing and retirement adequacy.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme
sections.summary: The Government announced the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme providing up to $6,000 over six months to the involuntarily unemployed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Last month, the Government announced the new SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme, which will provide up to $6,000 over six months to those who have made involuntarily unemployed.

sections.label: Platform workers representation and sector resilience
sections.summary: Platform workers should have organised means to negotiate collectively, and the Government was asked how the Bill impacts the platform service ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: But they also hope that the society would not see them as a forgotten group and also appreciate their fair share of contributions in the service that they provide to the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: They should also have the organised means and representation to collectively negotiate and bargain with the platform operators so as to safeguard the interest of the fellow platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Many of the platform operators are still running operating losses and counting on money from investors to keep the operations going.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: With that in mind, can I ask the Senior Minister of State how would the changes envisaged in this Bill impact the overall ecosystem of the platform service?

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: As this sector does create employment and income, and also provide useful flexible work arrangements, besides the Platform Workers Bill, how can the Government help to strengthen the resilience and robustness of this sector?

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my questions, Sir, I support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: They are now more than 70,000 platform workers in Singapore as of 2023.

sections.label: CPF contribution rates alignment
sections.summary: The Bill aligns CPF contribution rates for platform workers and companies with those of regular employees and employers for workers born on or after 1 January 1995.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This Bill recognises the need to ensure equitable pay for our platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We support the change made by the Bill to align the CPF contribution rates for platform workers and platform companies to those of regular employees and employers for platform workers born on or after 1 January 1995.

sections.label: Monitoring incentives and work injury compensation
sections.summary: Government should monitor that platform companies do not reduce incentives to offset CPF costs, and companies must pay work injury compensation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Employer CPF should not be another reason for platform companies to reduce incentives for platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Hence, once the CPF contribution regime is implemented in 2025, the Government should closely monitor the situation to ensure that platform companies are not reducing incentives or earnings rates for platform workers to offset the higher labour cost that they need to shoulder by paying CPF contributions for platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As such, we are glad that one of the key changes made in the Bill is that platform companies must now pay compensation to platform workers for work injuries at the same scope and level as employees are entitled.

sections.label: PSP welcomes Platform Workers Bill
sections.summary: PSP welcomes the Platform Workers Bill as a first step, noting over 70,000 platform workers in Singapore as of 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   The Progress Singapore Party (PSP) welcomes the introduction of the Platform Workers Bill as an important first step in improving the welfare of platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: There are now more than 70,000 platform workers in Singapore, as of 2023.

sections.label: CPF rates and platform companies
sections.summary: PSP supports aligning CPF rates for younger platform workers and asks if companies committed not to cut incentives or earnings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: On equitable pay for our platform workers, PSP supports the change made by the Bill to align the CPF contribution rates for platform workers and platform companies to those of regular employees and employers, for platform workers born on or after 1 January 1995.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The opt-in regime for older platform workers also meets the desire of many older platform workers to opt out of CPF contributions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, in order to ascertain that this change will really benefit the platform workers, we would like to ask the Government if it has gotten the commitment from the platform companies that they will not reduce incentives or earnings rates for platform workers to offset their increased costs from paying Employer CPF contributions?

sections.label: Minimum base fare proposal
sections.summary: PSP says platform companies and work associations should work towards a minimum base fare based on a $2,250 monthly living wage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For example, the PSP’s view is that platform companies and platform work associations should work towards an appropriate minimum base fare, calculated with reference to our proposed living wage of $2,250 per month, before CPF contributions, for 44 hours of work per week.

sections.label: New hybrid worker category
sections.summary: The Bill first legislates protection for freelancers, creates a hybrid worker category, and allows representation by platform work associations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: First, it is the first time in history that we have a specific legislation protecting freelancers and, in this case, vulnerable platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Second, we are creating a new hybrid category of "workers" through this piece of legislation: not exactly employees in an employment relationship nor fully an independent contractor as they will enjoy certain "employment" rights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Third, we are also allowing them to be represented by platform work associations similar to unions.

sections.label: Digital voting for secret ballots
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Senior Minister of State to consider allowing platform work associations to use digital voting for secret ballots.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: This is not the case for platform work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I would, therefore, ask the Senior Minister of State to consider allowing platform work associations to use digital voting for secret ballots.

sections.label: MOM finalising subsidiary legislation
sections.summary: The speaker asks MOM to work with tripartite partners on subsidiary legislation, noting the Bill covers ride-hail and delivery workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I, therefore, ask MOM to work with our tripartite partners and various stakeholders when finalising the subsidiary legislation, to make the Platform Workers Act effective and useful for all stakeholders and partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: This Bill, as currently tabled, only looks to cover platform workers who fall under the ride-hail and delivery worker categories.

sections.label: Earnings definition and industrial action
sections.summary: Section 2 of the Bill defines earnings and excludes special expenses, and a question asks how MOM would determine industrial action by platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: One, section 2 of the Bill provides the definition of earnings and excludes special expenses from being classified as earnings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Two, how would MOM determine there was an industrial action by platform workers, given that platform workers are free to choose whether or not to work for any reason as well as when to work and which platform operator to work for, all on their own volition?

sections.label: Platform worker classes and agreements
sections.summary: Questions ask the Senior Minister of State to clarify classes of platform workers and whether agreement in section 5(1)(a) refers to the defined platform work agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State clarify what classes of platform workers there may be?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: And fifth, lastly, does agreement in section 5(1)(a) of the Platform Workers Bill refer specifically to the defined platform work agreement or does it include a broader range of agreements since the term platform work agreement is not used in section 5(1)(a)?

sections.label: NTUC representation and affiliation
sections.summary: Over 99% of trade union members are represented through NTUC and its affiliates, and 58 of 61 employee trade unions are NTUC-affiliated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Over 99% of trade union members in Singapore are represented through the NTUC and its affiliates; and 58 out of 61, or 95% of employee trade unions in Singapore are affiliated with NTUC, underscoring the near total monopoly that the NTUC has over the Labour Movement in Singapore.

sections.label: PAP MPs as union advisers
sections.summary: NTUC announced in 2017 that where possible all PAP MPs, including Cabinet Ministers, would be appointed as advisers in NTUC bodies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The NTUC announced in 2017 that, where possible, all PAP MPs, which include Cabinet Ministers, would be appointed as advisers in the unions, professional associations and guilds under NTUC.

sections.label: ILO Convention and Platform Workers Bill
sections.summary: ILO Convention No 87, not ratified by Singapore, stresses independence from public authorities, and the speaker supports the Platform Workers Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: ILO's Convention No 87, on Freedom of Association and Protection of the Right to Organise, which the Singapore Government has not ratified, stresses that workers and employers organisations must be independent from public authorities and free from government control or interference.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Turning to the Platform Workers Bill, Mr Speaker, I support this legislation, which seeks to enhance the representation of private hire drivers and delivery riders.

sections.label: Point of Order on speech
sections.summary: A Point of Order states that the first 10 minutes of Mr Gerald Giam's speech had nothing to do with the Platform Workers Bill and attacked the NTUC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: If I may, Mr Speaker, a Point of Order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I listened very carefully to Mr Gerald Giam's speech for the first 10 minutes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I humbly and respectfully submit to the Chair that the first 10 minutes had nothing to do with the Platform Workers Bill that is being debated today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It was predominantly an attack against the NTUC.

sections.label: Registrar refusing platform work associations
sections.summary: The registrar may refuse registration of a new platform work association if one already exists for that platform service, or cancel an existing registration under similar conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: Furthermore, the registrar of platform work association has the authority to refuse registration of a new platform work association if there is already an existing one for that platform service or even to cancel the registration of an existing platform work association under similar conditions.

sections.label: Recognition requires majority vote
sections.summary: The Bill proposes that recognition of a platform work association requires a majority vote from platform workers eligible to participate in the recognition process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: The Bill proposes that recognition of a platform work association would require a majority vote from platform workers eligible to participate in the recognition process.

sections.label: Executive committee binds members
sections.summary: Clause 40 lets the platform work association's executive committee bind all members to a collective agreement without ratification by members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: Clause 40 of the Bill allows the platform work association's executive committee to bind all members to a collective agreement without the need for ratification by the members.

sections.label: Platform companies contribute CPF
sections.summary: The Bill requires platform companies to contribute employers' CPF payments to their workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: The Bill also requires platform companies to contribute employers' CPF payments to their workers.

sections.label: NTUC and PAP symbiotic relationship
sections.summary: Affiliated unions choose this, and NTUC's symbiotic relationship with the PAP conveys workers' views and needs to its political partner so workers' interests are prioritised when it becomes ruling party.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: And every union that is affiliated to the NTUC chooses to do that.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: And the NTUC has a symbiotic relationship with the PAP so that we can convey the views and the needs of the workers to our political partner, so that when they become the ruling party, when they win the trust of Singaporeans and have the mandate to be the ruling party, that the interests of workers in this country will always be taken care of, be given great priority.

sections.label: Bill's origin questioned
sections.summary: The speaker asks where the Bill the other party supports comes from, describing a symbiotic relationship where both sides undermine and throw workers under the bus.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Look at the context in which we are debating today.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: This very Bill that your party is supporting, where does this come from?

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: This comes from a symbiotic relationship where both sides are trying to undermine and throw the workers under the bus?

sections.label: Fairness to unions and NTUC
sections.summary: The speaker calls for fairness to union leaders, unions and the NTUC, urging practical action.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: If we care for that fish in there, let us do something practical.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: This is my heartfelt response: be fair to our union leaders, be fair to our unions, be fair to the NTUC.

sections.label: Attack on NTUC and PAP
sections.summary: The speaker says Mr Giam's speech was essentially an attack on the NTUC and its symbiotic relationship with the PAP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Second point, I listened very carefully to what Mr Giam was saying for I think 60% or 70% of his speech – and it was essentially an attack on the NTUC and by extension, an attack on the NTUC's symbiotic relationship with the PAP.

sections.label: UK trade unions and Labour
sections.summary: Mr Gerald Giam studied UK trade unions; UK unions pay the Labour Party an annual fee and elect committee members and delegates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The hon Member Mr Gerald Giam said that he studied the trade unions relationship in the UK.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I am not sure if he realises that the trade unions in the UK actually pay an annual fee to the Labour Party.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In return, they elect 13 out of 39 members of the National Executive Committee and 50% of delegates to the Labour Party Conference.

sections.label: SATU and Barisan Socialist
sections.summary: SATU was aligned with the Barisan Socialist, which in 1988 folded into the WP.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: SATU was aligned with the Barisan Socialist and the Barisan Socialist in 1988 folded into the WP.

sections.label: Protection for unprotected people
sections.summary: The debate concerns people who lack protection and need it, and the Bill aims to give them that protection.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I would just bring the debate back to this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This is about people who do not have much protection and who need protection, and we are trying to get this Bill passed so that they can have that protection.

sections.label: Focus on the Bill
sections.summary: The speaker urges focusing on the Bill, which can do better for workers and gig workers and protect them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Let us focus on this Bill, because with this Bill, we can do better for our workers, our gig workers, and protect them.

sections.label: NTUC alignment with PAP
sections.summary: The passage states the NTUC is aligned to the PAP and is expected to remain aligned even after the PAP loses power.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: In any case, I think the whole thrust of what the Leader, Senior Minister of State Koh and Mr Yam had said earlier on is that the NTUC is aligned to the PAP and there is nothing usual in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: So, we expect that the NTUC would continue to be aligned with the PAP, even after the PAP loses power.

sections.label: Passing the platform workers Bill
sections.summary: The passage states there is a Bill to pass so that rights and protections can be conferred on platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But at the end of the day, it comes back to this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We have a Bill to pass and let us pass this Bill so that we can confer rights and protections on our platform workers.

sections.label: Commendable platform worker provisions
sections.summary: The passage states that provisions on mandatory CPF contributions, insurance coverage and dispute resolution mechanisms are commendable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The provisions on mandatory CPF contributions, insurance coverage and dispute resolution mechanisms are commendable.

sections.label: Skills upgrading not in Bill
sections.summary: The passage asks the Senior Minister of State to elaborate on why long-term measures such as continuous skills upgrading programmes were not included in the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State elaborate on why certain long-term measures, such as continuous skills upgrading programmes, were not included in this Bill?

sections.label: Bill compared with other jurisdictions
sections.summary: The passage asks the Senior Minister of State to share how the Bill compares with similar regulations in other jurisdictions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State share how this Bill compares with similar regulations in other jurisdictions?

sections.label: Impact on transport and food costs
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Bill will significantly impact transport and food costs for residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will this Bill significantly impact transport and food costs for residents?

sections.label: Balancing flexibility and protections
sections.summary: The passage states a balance must be struck between preserving flexibility that attracts individuals to the sector and providing essential protections for their well-being and livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As we continue to navigate these uncharted waters, we must strike a balance between preserving the flexibility that attracts individuals to this sector and at the same time providing essential protections that safeguard their well-being and livelihoods.

sections.label: Career development and Bill clarity
sections.summary: The passage calls for addressing long-term career development for older and senior workers and urges the Senior Minister of State to provide clarity on the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Furthermore, we need to address long-term career development, particularly for older and senior workers, by providing avenues for skills upgrading and facilitating transitions to more sustainable career paths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I also urge the Senior Minister of State to provide clarity on how this Bill compares with international regulations, elaborate on potential unintended consequences and mitigation strategies, and commit to continuous engagement with stakeholders throughout the implementation process.

sections.label: Insurance coverage and road security
sections.summary: The passage states that with the Bill, workers will feel greater security from insurance coverage and more at ease navigating the roads without unfair penalties or abuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: With this Bill, they will feel greater security knowing they have insurance coverage – a safety net we hope they never have to use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: They will feel more at ease navigating the roads, knowing they will not be unfairly penalised or subjected to abuse from impatient customers.

sections.label: Union-like powers for platform associations
sections.summary: The passage states the Bill is a landmark in labour laws because it gives registered platform work associations union-like powers to negotiate with platform operators on fair treatment, sustainable earnings and work safety.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill is a landmark in labour laws because it accords registered platform work associations with union-like powers to negotiate with platform operators on work areas such as fair treatment, sustainable earnings and work safety.

sections.label: Food delivery worker accident poll
sections.summary: The passage states an Institute of Policy Studies 2022 poll found one in three food delivery workers had at least one accident requiring medical attention, with risks rising for those working longer hours and earning more.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: An Institute of Policy Studies 2022 poll found that one in three food delivery workers have been in at least one accident that required medical attention, and accident risks increased for those who worked longer hours and earned more.

sections.label: Platform operators' injury financial responsibility
sections.summary: The passage states the Bill assigns platform operators financial responsibility for injury, incapacity or death of a platform worker associated with performing a platform job.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill also assigns to platform operators, financial responsibility for injury, incapacity or death of a platform worker associated with performing a platform job.

sections.label: WSH Act code of practice
sections.summary: The amended WSH Act stipulates a code of practice for platform operators, now open for public feedback.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The amended WSH Act also stipulates a code of practice for platform operators; the code is now open for public feedback.

sections.label: CPF contributions for platform workers
sections.summary: From 1 January next year, platform operators must contribute to provident funds of platform workers born on or after 1995 and those who opt in.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To recap, from 1 January next year, platform operators must contribute to the provident funds of platform workers who are born on or after 1995 as well as those who opt-in to the CPF scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I also appreciate the raised income threshold as well as the higher percent Government support for the PCTS scheme that would benefit more platform workers to larger extent.

sections.label: Platform operators AI Verify participation
sections.summary: One requirement is for platform operators to participate in Singapore's AI governance testing framework, AI Verify.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One, is to require platform operators to participate in Singapore’s AI governance testing framework, AI Verify.

sections.label: LTA standards for operational disruptions
sections.summary: LTA's move to introduce standards for managing operational disruptions for taxi and ride-hail operators assigns responsibility and accountability to platform operators.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Land Transport Authority’s (LTA's) move to introduce standards for managing operational disruptions for all taxi and ride-hail operators is a positive step because it assigns responsibility and accountability to platform operators.

sections.label: AI validation and income protection
sections.summary: One measure requires platform operators to periodically validate AI systems for fairness; another provides platform workers income protection during extended app outages.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One, by requiring platform operators to periodically validate their AI systems to ensure fairness.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Two, by providing platform workers with some income protection in event of extended platform app outage.

sections.label: NTUC platform work associations
sections.summary: NTUC announced its intention to register platform work associations representing taxi drivers, private hire vehicle drivers and platform delivery workers if the Bill is passed.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Platform workers have shared with our associations their worries of platform operators diffusing the cost of Bill compliance among platform workers under the cloak of less-than-transparent earnings statement and/ or brute force implementation.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, last month, the NTUC announced its intention to register platform work associations that represent taxi drivers, private hire vehicle drivers and platform delivery workers should this Bill be passed.

sections.label: Tripartite set-ups for platform sector
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry plans to re-introduce tripartite set-ups for discussions between the sectoral platform work association and platform operators on livelihood issues.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Does the Ministry plan to re-introduce tripartite set-ups that can facilitate discussions between the sectoral platform work association and platform operators on livelihood issues impacting the sector and its workers?

sections.label: Platform worker death and disability coverage
sections.summary: A 2022 Advisory Committee report found platform operators' typical death or total permanent disability coverage is largely $10,000 to $30,000, versus WICA's $289,000 limit for employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to the 2022 report by the Advisory Committee on Platform Workers, the typical coverage for death or total permanent disability of platform workers provided by platform operators lies largely in the $10,000 to $30,000 range.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: This pales in comparison to the limit of $289,000 for employees under the WICA.

sections.label: Platform worker fatalities and accidents
sections.summary: The Advisory Committee report found eight work-related traffic fatalities among platform workers from January 2021 to October 2022, and an IPS study found one in three food delivery workers had an accident needing medical attention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The report by the Advisory Committee on Platform Workers found that from January 2021 to October 2022, there were eight work-related traffic fatalities among platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Earlier, the Senior Minister of State also cited a 2022 study by the Institute of Policy Studies, which found that one in three food delivery workers has been in at least one accident that required medical attention.

sections.label: NTUC feedback and platform worker protection
sections.summary: NTUC received feedback that some private hire vehicle drivers do not declare accompanying children below seven, causing wasted trips, and the Bill aims to provide platform workers financial protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: NTUC has received feedback from private hire vehicle drivers that some customers do not declare when they have accompanying children below the age of seven.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Only taxis can ferry such passengers without a child seat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: So, by failing to declare, it leads to a wasted trip for our platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: As merchants and senders, we can pack our food and goods properly and honestly declare to the platform the correct weight and size of the item that we intend to send.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement has and will continue to champion the interests of our platform workers because every platform worker matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This Bill represents extensive discussions and aims to provide platform workers with financial protection covering work injuries, housing and retirement adequacy.

sections.label: Platform workers' expense-to-income ratio
sections.summary: A 2023 DBS study found platform workers' expense-to-income ratio has risen to 112%, meaning they spend more than they earn.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: A 2023 DBS study found that platform workers' expense-to-income ratio has risen to 112%, meaning they are spending more than they earn.

sections.label: PCTS income cap basis
